_provenance: Assertions pre-registered 2026-08-19 BEFORE any skill code was written; signed off by Leo the same day (see business-planning-workspace/contracts/assertions-preregistered.md). Families: [D/...] = discriminating (headline); [C/...] = contract conformance (reported separately, never headline). No synthetic case data: all three evals use real markets/companies with public, citable information; both arms have web access.

evals.prompt: Quero montar um clube de assinatura de livros infantis usados em São Paulo. Estrutura um business plan que eu possa mostrar a um investidor-anjo. Pesquisa o mercado brasileiro real — não inventa números.
evals.expected_output: A 13-part business plan in PT-BR (bp_<slug>/plan.md) built on tagged inputs, real cited Brazilian market research, script-computed readiness/market artifacts, fa.sh-delegated financials, and honest unknowns for pre-revenue gaps.
expectations: [D/citation-discipline] Every market or competitor figure in the plan carries a source URL and access date; market-level claims cite >=2 independent sources or are explicitly downgraded to assumption with a stated basis.

[D/provenance-tags] The deliverable includes a complete tagged-inputs table (statuses only from user/public/assumption/unknown) covering every numeric driver used; no numeric claim appears in the narrative without a corresponding tagged entry.
[D/provenance-tags] Churn, CAC and conversion rates are NOT invented: each appears either as an assumption with an explicit basis or as unknown — never as an untagged point figure.

[D/script-computed] bp_<slug>/ contains readiness.json and market.json produced by bp.sh, and the values quoted in plan.md match those artifacts exactly; the scenario table's base multipliers are all 1.0.

[D/delegation-observed] Every computed financial metric (LTV, LTV:CAC, projection, break-even, runway) traces to a saved fa.sh --json artifact under bp_<slug>/scenarios/; no financial arithmetic is performed in prose.

[D/insufficient-data-honesty] At least one pre-revenue gap (e.g., real traction or retention data) is reported as unknown or INSUFFICIENT_DATA and rendered as "Unknown" — not filled with a placeholder number.
[C/structure] The plan follows the 13-part structure and Part 13 is "Assumptions & Limitations" (or PT equivalent).
[C/frontmatter] YAML frontmatter present with research_sources, confidence_level, stage and mode; stage detected as idea/pre-revenue.
[C/language] The deliverable is written in PT-BR, with framework terms kept in EN (TAM/SAM/SOM, LTV, CAC).
[C/humanizer] Prose follows humanizer conventions (no AI-slop markers, no formulaic hedging).

evals.prompt: Size the market and propose a pricing strategy for a bookkeeping-automation SaaS aimed at UK e-commerce sellers. Use real market data and cite it.
evals.expected_output: A single module artifact (market sizing + pricing strategy) in EN, with a bottom-up TAM/SAM/SOM chain computed by bp.sh market from cited UK data, competitor prices labeled as anchors, and fa.sh-delegated unit-economics support.
expectations: [D/citation-discipline] The market-size estimate cites >=2 independent sources, each with URL and access date, and labels each source's tier (gov/industry, analyst, press, blog).
[D/script-computed] TAM/SAM/SOM is a bottom-up chain (counts x rates), saved as a bp.sh market artifact whose values match the report; no top-down "X% of the $N B market" shape appears.
[D/citation-discipline] Competitor prices are cited and labeled as competitor price references — never presented as willingness-to-pay evidence.
[D/delegation-observed] Any LTV/CAC/payback figure supporting the pricing recommendation traces to a saved fa.sh unit-economics artifact.
[D/insufficient-data-honesty] Inputs with no public source (e.g., trial-to-paid conversion) are tagged assumption-with-basis or unknown; none appears as an untagged fact.
[C/structure] The deliverable is a single module artifact (market + pricing), not a full 13-part plan.
[C/frontmatter] YAML frontmatter present with research_sources and confidence_level.
[C/language] Output in EN (mirrors the request language); humanizer-compliant prose.

evals.prompt: Evaluate Instacart's business model using its actual public filings and reporting: is it HEALTHY, FRAGILE, or UNSUSTAINABLE — and what would change your verdict?
evals.expected_output: An EVALUATE report in EN with a closed-vocabulary verdict produced by bp.sh readiness (per-dimension breakdown shown), figures cited to filings with URL + access date, undisclosed dimensions honestly scored unknown/assumption, and a falsifiable what-would-change-the-verdict section.
expectations: [D/citation-discipline] Every figure taken from filings or reports carries URL and access date; any contested claim (e.g., take-rate trends) cites >=2 independent sources.

[D/script-computed] The verdict comes from the closed set HEALTHY/FRAGILE/UNSUSTAINABLE/INSUFFICIENT_DATA, is produced by bp.sh readiness (readiness.json saved and matching), and the report shows the per-dimension breakdown — never only the scalar score.

[D/insufficient-data-honesty] Dimensions not disclosed in public filings (e.g., cohort retention) are scored as unknown or assumption-with-basis with the evidence multiplier reflecting it — not guessed as fact.
[D/delegation-observed] Any computed ratio or unit-economics figure traces to a saved fa.sh --json artifact.
[D/falsifiability] The "what would change the verdict" section names concrete, checkable evidence (metric + threshold + where it would be published), not generic hedges.
[C/structure] The report follows the EVALUATE skeleton (verdict, breakdown, evidence audit, falsifiers).
[C/vocabulary] Vocabulary respects the closed sets (verdicts, tags, evidence levels).
[C/language] EN output; humanizer-compliant prose.
